extracted.intended_audience: Users of Isabelle/HOL (proof engineers, formal-methods practitioners, library authors and advanced theorem-prover users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and command-level requirements for derived specification elements (records, typedefs, quotients, lifting/transfer) and proof tools in Isabelle/HOL. Covers semantic obligations, automation triggers, attributes, and configuration options used when defining types and proving/transporting theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard conversions for selectors/updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard conversions for selectors or updates applied to record constructor terms are made part of the default Simplifier context; these rules are available as t.simps too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus proofs by reduction of basic operations merely require the simp method without further arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic simplification of selectors on updated records
rubrics_metrics.description: Selectors applied to updated records are automatically reduced by an internal simplification procedure, which is also part of the standard Simplifier setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can rely on the simplifier to reduce selector expressions on updated records in routine proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inject equations declared as iff rules (t.iifs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inject equations of a form analogous to (x,y) = (x',y') ≡ x = x' ∧ y = y' are declared to the Simplifier and Classical Reasoner as iff rules. These rules are available as t.iifs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes reasoning about injectivity and decomposition of constructor equalities automatic in many proof contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction rule for record equality (t.equality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction rule for record equality analogous to componentwise equality is declared to the Simplifier, and as the basic rule context 'intro?'. The rule is called t.equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t.equality can be used by proof methods expecting an introduction rule; it is registered to simplify equality reasoning over records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical constructor representations for record expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations of arbitrary record expressions as canonical constructor terms are provided both in cases and induct format (cf. the generic proof methods 'cases' and 'induct').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The generic proof methods are smart enough to pick the most sensible rule according to the type of the indicated record expression; users typically apply '(cases r)' on a proof problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derived record operations not auto-expanded
rubrics_metrics.description: The derived record operations t.make, t.fields, t.extend, t.truncate are not treated automatically, but usually need to be expanded by hand, using the collective fact t.defs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proofs depend on these derived operations, explicitly expand them (via t.defs) rather than expecting automatic unfolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: typedef requires non-emptiness proof
rubrics_metrics.description: typedef (α1,...,αn) t = A defines a new type t from the set A over an existing type. Non-emptiness of A needs to be proven on the spot (∃ x. x ∈ A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The on-the-spot proof of ∃x. x ∈ A is required to make the typedef usable; it turns the internal conditional characterization into usable theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: typedef 'overloaded' option
rubrics_metrics.description: The '(overloaded)' option allows the typedef specification to depend on constants that are not (yet) specified and thus left open as parameters (e.g. type-class parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '(overloaded)' when the representing set must refer to yet-unspecified constants; this makes the typedef act parametrically with respect to those constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-theory typedef restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a local theory specification, the newly introduced type constructor cannot depend on parameters or assumptions of the context: this is syntactically impossible in HOL. The non-emptiness proof may formally depend on local assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that typedefs inside local theories are limited: you cannot make the new type constructor itself depend on local parameters, although the existence proof can use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: typedef provides Rep_t and Abs_t morphisms and instantiated theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: For typedef t = A the newly introduced type t is accompanied by a pair of morphisms (Rep_t, Abs_t) relating it to the representing set. Generic locale theorems (type_declaration.Rep, Abs_inverse, etc.) are instantiated accordingly (e.g. Rep_t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided Rep/Abs morphisms and the instantiated theorems (Rep_inject, Abs_inject, Rep_cases/Rep_induct, Abs_cases/Abs_induct) for automated reasoning; many of these are already declared as set/type rules for methods like 'cases' and 'induct'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer datatype for trivial enumerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trivial constructions (e.g. pulling a finite enumeration into existence) are better done with derived specification mechanisms such as 'datatype' instead of primitive typedef.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using 'datatype' avoids redoing basic definitions and proofs that typedef would require from primitives.

rubrics_metrics.name: functor: mapper term type pattern requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The given term m for 'functor' is considered as mapper for the corresponding type constructor and must conform to the following type pattern: m :: σ1 ⇒ ... ⇒ σk ⇒ (αn) t ⇒ (βn) t, where σ1..σk is a subsequence of α1 ⇒ β1, β1 ⇒ α1, ..., αn ⇒ βn, βn ⇒ αn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the mapper m has the required polymorphic relational shape so that the functorial structure properties can be registered and used by other packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotient_type requires equivalence (or partial equivalence) proof
rubrics_metrics.description: quotient_type defines a new quotient type τ given a raw type and a (partial) equivalence relation; the package requires the user to prove that the relation is an equivalence (equivp) unless the user specifies 'partial' in which case the obligation is part_equivp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use 'partial' fewer automatic facts follow; proving full equivalence yields stronger automation and transfer rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotient_type defines rep_τ/abs_τ and integrates with Lifting
rubrics_metrics.description: quotient_type defines the injection rep_τ and its inverse abs_τ (unless alternative names are provided) and internally proves a Quotient theorem and sets up the Lifting package (setup_lifting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: quotient_type automates registration with Lifting/Transfer, so quotient types are ready for lifting and transfer unless low-level customization is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: setup_lifting low-level mode obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: setup_lifting's low-level mode requires as first argument a quotient theorem Quotient R Abs Rep T. Optional second argument reﬂp R (certifying R is total) and an optional parametricity theorem can be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing reﬂp R and parametricity theorems yields stronger transfer rules; low-level mode is for manual setup when automation is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: setup_lifting automated modes for typedef/quotient_type
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new subtype is defined by typedef, or a quotient by quotient_type, setup_lifting can be invoked in a mode that uses the corresponding type_declaration or Quotient theorem as an argument; the command internally proves the Quotient theorem and registers it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users generally need not manually prove Quotient theorems for new types if they used typedef or quotient_type; setup_lifting will handle the registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift_definition semantics and respectfulness obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: lift_definition f :: τ is t defines a new function f with an abstract type τ in terms of a corresponding operation t on a representation type; the command opens a proof and the user must discharge a respectfulness proof obligation. A respectfulness theorem f.rsp and a transfer rule f.transfer are generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For type copies the obligation is discharged automatically. The command builds an F combining Abs/Rep and generates transfer/rep/abs equations as appropriate; parametricity can be specified to get stronger transfer rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift_declaration code-generation integration and constraints (code_dt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration with code generation: for subtypes lift_definition uses f.rep_eq as a code equation, but due to code generator limitations f.rep_eq cannot be used if the subtype occurs inside result type. The flag code_dt invokes an extension enabling code execution if the return type τ meets inductive conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return type τ must either be a type variable, or τ = τ1...τn κ where κ is an abstract type constructor and τ1..τn do not contain abstract types, or κ is a (co)datatype with constructor argument types free of non-free datatypes/function types. Use code_dt when necessary for code generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generated code/correspondence theorems (f.rep_eq, f.abs_eq)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each constant defined through trivial quotients (type copies or subtypes) f.rep_eq is generated (code certificate); for total quotients f.abs_eq is generated (unconditional equation defining f using abstraction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equations are used by the code generator and by normalization; be aware of their presence and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: lifting_forget and lifting_update manage lifting setup bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Lifting package is set up for a new abstract type τ, the package defines a bundle τ.lifting that includes Lifting setup. lifting_update τ.lifting stores transfer rules in the bundle; lifting_forget τ.lifting deletes set-up and transfer rules for τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lifting_update to preserve the lifting configuration and lifting_forget to hide type construction details or remove lifting setup; bundles can be included later if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: quot_map attribute (register quotient maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: quot_map registers a quotient map theorem showing how to 'lift' quotients over type constructors (e.g. Quotient R Abs Rep T =⇒ Quotient (rel_set R) (image Abs) (image Rep) (rel_set T)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is often proved automatically when the involved type is BNF without dead variables; it enables lifting across type constructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: relator_eq_onp attribute (hide eq_onp via predicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: relator_eq_onp registers a theorem that shows that a relator applied to an equality restricted by a predicate P (eq_onp P) equals a predicator applied to P. This allows the package to hide eq_onp from users in respectfulness theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatically proved for BNF types without dead variables; helps produce user-readable respectfulness statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: relator_mono attribute (monotonicity of relators)
rubrics_metrics.description: relator_mono registers a property describing monotonicity of a relator (e.g. A ≤ B =⇒ rel_set A ≤ rel_set B). Needed for stronger transfer rules and the reflexivity prover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatically available for BNF types without dead variables; register manually otherwise to improve transfer generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: relator_distr attribute (distributivity of relator composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: relator_distr registers distributivity properties of relation composition and a relator (e.g. rel_set R ◦◦ rel_set S = rel_set (R ◦◦ S)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prove stronger transfer rules; when equality does not hold unconditionally the user can specify directions separately. Requires relator_mono to be registered first.

rubrics_metrics.name: transfer method: replace goals guided by transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The transfer method replaces the current subgoal with a logically equivalent one that uses different types and constants, guided by the database of transfer rules. Goals are generalized over all free variables by default; transfer fixing (e.g. transfer fixing: x y z) can override this for particular variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transfer to move statements between abstract and representation types. Be aware of default generalization; fix variables when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: transfer (strong variant) for logically stronger replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: transfer' is a variant that allows replacing a subgoal with one that is logically stronger (rather than equivalent). Example: convert an equality on a quotient type to equality on the underlying raw type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stronger variant when the transported goal should be a stronger fact (e.g. replace an equiv relation by actual equality on representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: transfer_prover assists deriving transfer rules for new constants
rubrics_metrics.description: transfer_prover aids proving a transfer rule for a new constant provided the constant is defined in terms of other constants that already have transfer rules; apply it after unfolding the constant definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transfer_prover to derive transfer rules compositionally; see Transfer_Debug examples for strategy (transfer_prover = transfer_prover_start, transfer_step+, transfer_prover_end).

rubrics_metrics.name: transfer_rule attribute: maintain transfer rule collection
rubrics_metrics.description: transfer_rule attribute maintains rules relating constants at two different types (polymorphic instances or abstract/raw correspondences). Lemmas with predicates-on-relations may be registered similarly. Preservation of predicates (bi_unique, bi_total, left_total, right_unique, right_total) with respect to a relator is proved automatically if the involved type is BNF without dead variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register transfer rules for operations you want the transfer package to exploit. Many useful transfer rules are auto-registered for BNF types; otherwise manually supply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: transfer_domain_rule attribute: specify domain predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: transfer_domain_rule maintains rules that specify the domain of a transfer relation by a predicate (e.g. Domainp ZN = (λx. x ≥ 0)). These rules help produce more readable transferred goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register domain predicates for transfer relations to avoid awkward or unreadable transferred goals involving domain side-conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: relator_eq and relator_domain attributes for transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: relator_eq collects identity laws for relators (e.g. rel_set (=) = (=)) used by transfer to infer transfer rules on the fly. relator_domain collects rules describing domains of relators by predicators (e.g. Domainp (rel_set T) = (λA. Ball A (Domainp T))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes are auto-populated for BNF types without dead variables; otherwise register needed lemmas to enable transfer's inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old-style quotient commands and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: quotient_definition defines a constant on the quotient type; print_quotmapsQ3/print_quotientsQ3/print_quotconsts print quotient maps/quotients/constants. Methods like lifting, lifting_setup, descending, descending_setup, partiality_descending, regularize, injection, cleaning, quot_lifted, etc., provide heuristics and steps for lifting proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these methods to carry out old-style quotient lifting workflows; lifting attempts heuristics to solve regularization, injection and cleaning subgoals while lifting_setup leaves them unsolved for manual handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: lifting/descending method behaviors (regularization, injection, cleaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: lifting matches the current goal with a raw theorem to be lifted producing three subgoals: regularization, injection and cleaning. lifting tries heuristics to solve them; lifting_setup leaves the three subgoals unsolved. descending/descending_setup try to guess a raw statement that would lift to the current subgoal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on lifting for automated attempts; use lifting_setup or descending variants when you need finer control or when heuristics are insufficient. partiality_descending is for partial equivalence quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: quot_lifted and caution about automatic transport
rubrics_metrics.description: quot_lifted attribute tries to automatically transport the theorem to the quotient type using all defined quotients and quotient constants; it often produces undesired results or theorems that cannot be lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quot_lifted with caution; inspect results and prefer targeted lifting using explicit quot_thm or lifting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: quot_respect and quot_preserve attributes and quot_thm
rubrics_metrics.description: quot_respect and quot_preserve declare a theorem as a respectfulness or preservation theorem respectively, stored in the local theory and used by injection and cleaning methods. quot_thm declares a quotient extension theorem used to allow quotienting inside container types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare respectfulness/preservation/quotion-extension theorems to guide lifting heuristics when working with container or higher-order types.

rubrics_metrics.name: solve_direct/try0/try/sledgehammer proof tools semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: solve_direct checks whether current subgoals can be solved directly by an existing theorem. try0 attempts a combination of standard proof methods (auto, simp, blast, etc.). try attempts to prove or disprove a subgoal using a combination of provers and disprovers (solve_direct, quickcheck, try0, sledgehammer, nitpick). sledgehammer attempts to prove a subgoal using external automatic provers (resolution provers and SMT solvers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use try/try0 for quick local automation, solve_direct to find immediate theorem matches, and sledgehammer to call external ATPs; consult the Sledgehammer manual for advanced options.

rubrics_metrics.name: sledgehammer_params persistent configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: sledgehammer_params changes sledgehammer configuration options persistently at the theory level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust sledgehammer parameters when you want persistent behavior across invocations (e.g. prover selection, timeouts, relevance filters).

rubrics_metrics.name: value and values evaluation modes and evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: value t evaluates and prints a term; evaluation is tried first using ML, falling back to normalization by evaluation. Evaluators like 'simp' (symbolic simpliﬁcation), 'nbe' (normalization by evaluation) and 'code' (code generation in SML) can be selected. values t enumerates a set comprehension by evaluation and prints values up to a given number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an appropriate evaluator via square brackets when you need symbolic simplification, NBE normalization, or code-based evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck for counterexample search and its modes
rubrics_metrics.description: quickcheck tests the current goal for counterexamples using assignments for free variables. By default quickcheck uses exhaustive testing; testers available are exhaustive, random, and narrowing. Options include tester, size, genuine_only, abort_potential, eval, iterations, no_assms, locale, timeout, default_type, report, use_subtype, quiet, verbose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure quickcheck options to control search strategy, size limits, whether to abort on potential counterexamples, evaluation of terms under found assignments, and verbosity. Use 'genuine_only' to filter spurious counterexamples and 'use_subtype' to lift conjectures to registered subtypes automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: nitpick for counterexample/finite model search
rubrics_metrics.description: nitpick is another tool for finding counterexamples / models; nitpick_params persistently configure its behavior and nitpick supports various search strategies and backends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nitpick in combination with quickcheck and sledgehammer to diagnose incorrect propositions; consult nitpick documentation for backend selection and scope control.

rubrics_metrics.name: find_unused_assms to detect redundant assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: find_unused_assms searches proof context to find unused assumptions in a goal or structured proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run find_unused_assms to tidy proofs and remove redundant premises that are not needed by the proof methods.
